schemaVersion.description:
On-disk format version of this project template (`.evatemplate`). Absent on

AiObjectClassifierSettings.description:
Classifies objects with a model trained in the AI training dialog (an
`.evamodel` file).

Every object found so far that matches the input classes is scored on
its own, with the same features as in training - for the ring features
the ring around the object is measured here, as in training. The predicted class is
mapped to one of this project's classes and applied as set under
**Match handling** - the same input selection as **Classify Objects**,
but the class comes from the model's prediction instead of a fixed rule.

A predicted class without a mapping leaves the object untouched (like
unmapped classes of the pixel classifier stay background): map only the
classes you care about.

inputClasses.description:
Restrict classification to objects that already carry one of these classes

Only ROIs that have been assigned at least one of the listed classes by a prior
pipeline step will be evaluated by the model.
Leave empty to select the objects by their segmentation class only.
With neither input classes nor a segmentation class the step does nothing.

matchHandling.description:
What to do with object class labels after prediction

- **AddOutputClassIfMatch** - append the mapped class alongside the object's existing classes.
- **ReclassifyIfMatch** - clear every class the object carries and assign only the mapped class.

modelPath.description: Path to a trained object classifier model, saved from the AI training dialog.

originSegmentation.description:
Apply only to objects with this given segmentation class

The segmentation class value is assigned to each pixel in the image
after a Threshold, Pixel classifier or AI classifier.
Leave empty to select the objects by their input classes only.
With input classes too, an object must match both. Alone it also
selects objects without a class left - the way to bring objects an
earlier step removed back.

segmentationMapping.description: Maps the model's predicted classes to this project's object classes.

AiSegmentationUnetUNetOutputModeSettings.description:
How a multi-channel U-Net output should be turned into a single foreground
probability map. Ignored for single-channel outputs, which are always
treated as already-activated foreground probabilities.

oneOf.description:
Channels are mutually-exclusive class scores (e.g. a background/foreground
classification head). `softmax` is applied over the channel dimension
first, then the channel at `foreground_channel` is taken as the
foreground probability.

Channels are independent, already-activated probability maps — e.g. a
foreground-mask channel plus a separate boundary channel, as produced by
boundary-aware models (mask + boundary heads are *not* mutually
exclusive, so they must never be put through a softmax together). The
channel at `foreground_channel` is used directly.

BlurSettings.description:
Smooths an image by averaging pixel intensities within a local neighborhood.

This algorithm applies a uniform box filter where every pixel within the moving
window contributes equally to the final value. It is a computationally fast
method used for general image smoothing, blending variations, and rapid noise
suppression where edge precision is less critical.

kernelSize.description:
The size of the blur matrix.

Must be an odd number (e.g., 3, 5, 7)

CellposeSettings.description:
Instance segmentation using a Cellpose-SAM model

[AI Cellpose Segmentation] -> [Extract Objects]

Object segmentation using Cellpose-SAM model which can be downloaded from
https://evanalyzer.org/downloads/#ai-models

Cellpose-SAM is a biological segmentation model that integrates the pretrained transformer
architecture of Meta's Segment Anything Model (SAM) with the Cellpose framework to accurately
predict vector flow fields for dense cellular structures.
By combining these methods, it achieves "superhuman generalization," outperforming the average
accuracy of human annotators and reaching near-optimal cell masking performance. [1]

[1] Pachitariu, M., Rariden, M., & Stringer, C. (2025). Cellpose-SAM: superhuman generalization for cellular segmentation. bioRxiv. doi.org

cellposePostprocessing.description:
Build the objects from the flows exactly like Cellpose does: pixels
follow the interpolated flows, an object only starts where more than
10 pixels end up together, and pixels that reach no such spot become
background. Off, every spot any pixel ends up at starts an object,
which can join touching cells. Cellpose also fills the holes inside
each object - add a Fill Object Holes step after this one for that.

flowThreshold.description:
Flow error threshold: an object whose shape doesn't match the flows
the model predicted (mean squared error above this value) is removed.
Increase to keep more objects, decrease to keep only clean ones. `0`
disables the check (Cellpose's default is `0.4`).

inputChannels.description:
Number of input channels the model expects. The grayscale image goes in
channel 0; any further channels are zero-filled. Cellpose-SAM's
patch-embedding convolution only has weights for up to 3 input
channels: `2` (cytoplasm + optional nucleus) is standard, `1` is for
single-channel exports.

maxResize.description:
Longest image side, in pixels, the image is scaled down to before
segmentation; the masks are scaled back up to the original size
afterwards. Smaller values make large cells look like the cell sizes
the model was trained on and are faster. The scale is taken from the
full image, so every tile is scaled the same. `0` keeps the full
resolution (the Cellpose web demo uses `1000`).

minObjectSize.description:
Minimum object size, in pixels. After the dynamics, any instance smaller
than this is removed (its pixels become background). `0` disables the filter.

modelPath.description: Path to a TorchScript-exported Cellpose model (`torch.jit.script`/`torch.jit.trace`).

probabilityThreshold.description:
Cell probability above which a pixel takes part in the flow dynamics and
can be assigned to an object. The raw cell-probability logits are passed
through a sigmoid first, so this is a probability in `[0, 1]` (Cellpose's
default logit threshold of `0` corresponds to `0.5`).

replicateGrayChannel.description:
Copy the gray image into every input channel instead of filling the
extra channels with zeros. With `input_channels = 3` this matches
Cellpose run on an RGB image whose channels are (nearly) equal.

segmentationClass.description:
The class assigned to pixels of every detected object. All other
pixels are assigned `SegmentationClass::BACKGROUND`.

ClassificationMappingSettings.description:
Maps one class the model was trained to predict to a class ID meaningful
in this project. Model class IDs are a snapshot taken at training time
(see `evanalyzer_cfg::ObjectClassLabel`'s doc comment) and aren't
guaranteed to line up with this project's own `ObjectClass` IDs - this is
the bridge between the two.

objectClass.description: Object class predicted by the classifier model.

outputClass.description:
The project's own object class objects predicted as `object_class`
are assigned.

ClassifyObjectsSettings.description:
Classifies ROIs based on morphological and intensity features.

This command applies rule-based classification logic to assign object classes
to extracted ROIs. Classification is performed using configurable criteria
including area, shape descriptors, and intensity statistics.

allowEdgeTouching.description: Whether object can touch image edge

inputClasses.description:
Restrict classification to objects that already carry one of these classes

Only ROIs that have been assigned at least one of the listed classes by a prior
pipeline step will be evaluated against the morphological and intensity criteria below.
Leave empty to select the objects by their segmentation class only.
With neither input classes nor a segmentation class the step does nothing.

intensityFilters.description:
Intensity criteria, e.g. "average in channel 1 brighter than 1200"

All filters must match (logical AND), like every other criterion of
this command. Combine an `Above` and a `Below` filter on the same
channel and metric to select an intensity range. Empty: no intensity
criterion.

matchHandling.description:
What to do with object class labels after criteria evaluation

Controls whether the output class is added or existing classes are removed,
and whether the action is triggered on a criteria **match** or a **non-match**:

- **AddOutputClassIfMatch** - append the output class to objects that pass the criteria.
- **AddOutputClassIfNotMatch** - append the output class to objects that fail the criteria.
- **RemoveInputClassIfMatch / NotMatch** - strip all input classes from matching / non-matching objects.
- **RemoveOutputClassIfMatch / NotMatch** - strip the output class from matching / non-matching objects.
- **RemoveAllClassesIfMatch / NotMatch** - clear every class label from matching / non-matching objects.

maxAspectRatio.description:
Maximum proportional relationship between an object's width and its height

This value is calculated by the object bounding box with and height and is defined with `a = with/height`.
The value is without unit in the range of 0 to MAX_F32

maxCircularity.description:
Circularity range: 0 = elongated, 1 = perfect circle

Circularity (sometimes called Isoperimetric Quotient) measures how efficiently a shape encloses its area relative to the length of its perimeter.
A circle is the mathematically perfect shape for maximizing area while minimizing perimeter.
It is calculated with `4*Pi*AreaSize / Perimeter^2`

maxEccentricity.description:
Eccentricity: 0 = perfect circle, 1 = line

Eccentricity is a metric that measures how much a shape deviates from being a perfect circle.
It imagines the shape as an ellipse and measures how far apart its focal points are.
It is calculated with `sqrt(1-(b/a)^2)`

maxFeret.description:
Maximum feret diameter threshold in selected unit (px or nm)

The absolute longest distance across the object at any angle.
Used to measure elongation or the maximum length of a particle.

In image processing and particle size analysis, the Feret diameter (often called the caliper diameter) is a metric used to measure the size of an irregular object.
It mimics the action of a slide caliper, measuring the distance between two parallel tangential lines bounding the object at a specific angle.
When analyzing objects or particles, applying Feret diameter thresholds allows you to filter out noise, classify objects by shape, or isolate specific structures based on their directional length rather than their total area.

maxSize.description:
Maximum size

Maximum size of the object in the selected unit: its area in 2D
(px² or nm²), its volume in 3D (px³ or nm³).

maxSolidity.description:
Maximum Solidity/Compactness: 0 = hollow, 1 = perfect convex

Solidity is a structural metric used in shape analysis to measure how "solid" or compact an object is.
It compares the actual area of an object to the area of its Convex Hull (the smallest convex polygon that can completely enclose the object,
often visualized as a rubber band stretched around the shape).

Solidity = 1.0: The object is perfectly convex (e.g., a perfect circle, a solid square, or an ellipse). It has no holes, indentations, or deep recesses.
Solidity < 1.0: The object has irregular boundaries, deep "bays," protrusions, or internal holes. The lower the value, the more jagged or structurally fragmented the object is.

The value is without unit in the range of 0 to MAX_F32

originSegmentation.description:
Apply only to objects with this given segmentation class

The segmentation class value is assigned to each pixel in the image

Leave empty to select the objects by their input classes only.
With input classes too, an object must match both. Alone it also

outputClass.description:
Class label assigned to (or removed from) objects by the chosen operation

Used as the target class for `AddOutputClass*` and `RemoveOutputClass*` operations.
Has no effect when the selected operation only manipulates input classes or clears all classes.

overlappingWith.description:
Additional criterion: the object must intersect an object carrying this class

If unset (the default) this filter is not applied. When set, an object only
satisfies the overall criteria if it also overlaps at least one object carrying this
class by at least `min_intersection_size`. Combine with e.g.
`RemoveAllClassesIfMatch` to drop objects that intersect another class's objects,
or `AddOutputClassIfMatch` to tag objects that do.

sizeUnit.description: Unit to use for object extraction

ColocalizeObjectsSettings.description:
Calculates spatial colocalization and intersections between specified object classes.

This command scans the object cache, groups objects by their designated classes,
and performs spatial overlap analysis. It records colocalization relationships
between intersecting entities and can optionally generate new child ROIs representing
the precise intersection regions.

allCombinations.description:
Record every pair that overlaps, also of objects that don't overlap
an object of each class: one step with A, B and C shows A∩B, A∩C,
B∩C and A∩B∩C in the results' partner columns. Off: only the objects
overlapping every other class record partners. "As" and the overlap
regions always need every class.

classForOverlappingAreas.description:
Class of the overlapping area if needed

If defined the overlapping coloc area is added as new object and labeled with this class

classesToColoc.description:
The classes whose objects must overlap (e.g. the ch1 and the ch2
spots): each object overlapping an object of every other class
records them as its partners - listed and counted in the results.

excludeClasses.description:
Classes an object must NOT overlap to be considered colocalized.

Exclude_classes is a blocklist — "even if an object matches everything else, throw it out if it also touches one of these classes."
Concretely: you're looking for objects that overlap every class in classes_to_coloc (say Class 1 and Class 2).
Without exclude_classes, any object satisfying that gets recorded as colocalized.
With exclude_classes: an object that overlaps 1 and 2 but also touches Class 3 gets dropped entirely - no colocalization recorded for it at all, even though it passed the 1-and-2 check.
So it's a "match A and B, but not C" filter

Example: "cells colocalizing with both a nucleus stain and a membrane stain, but exclude any that also overlap a dead-cell marker."

filterClasses.description:
Optional additional label filters.

Only classes which matches all of these filters are used for coloc calculation

markAs.description:
Optional: the class the colocalizing objects get (e.g. "ch1 with
ch2") - to count them per image or relate them to cells. `Unset`:
only the partners are recorded.

minColocSize.description: Minimum overlap to count objects as coloc - an area in 2D, a volume in 3D

multiplicity.description: Which overlapping objects count as partners.

sizeUnit.description: Size unit for the minimum coloc size

ColorFilterCommandSettings.description:
A command that filters an image based on a specific HSV color range.

Pixels falling outside the HSV range are masked
out by setting to black.

range.description: The HSV color bounds to be preserved by the filter.

ConnectedComponentsSettings.description:
Identifies and labels discrete objects within a binary or multi-class image.

[Preprocessing] -> [Segment/Threshold] -> [Fill Holes] -> [Connected Components] -> [Watershed] -> [Extract Objects]

DistanceTransformSettings.description:
A command that calculates the Euclidean Distance Map (EDM) of an f32 image.

This algorithm identifies pixels below a threshold as "background" and
calculates the distance of every "foreground" pixel to the nearest background pixel.

edgesAreBackground.description: If true, the pixels outside the image boundary are treated as background.

threshold.description: Values less than or equal to this are treated as background (distance = 0).

EdgeDetectionCannySettings.description:
Extracts structural boundaries and fine edges using the multi-stage Canny algorithm.

This algorithm identifies optimal edge locations by calculating spatial intensity
gradients, suppressing non-maximum pixel responses to thin lines down to 1-pixel width,
and applying a dual-threshold hysteresis loop to preserve weak edges connected
to strong ones while completely rejecting isolated noise.

kernelSize.description:
Size of the Gaussian smoothing kernel.

Must be an odd number (e.g., 3, 5). Larger values reduce
noise but can blur fine edge details.

thresholdMax.description:
Upper bound for hysteresis thresholding [0.0, 1.0].

Edges with a gradient intensity above this value are considered
"strong" and are automatically preserved.

thresholdMin.description:
Lower bound for hysteresis thresholding [0.0, 1.0].

Edges with a gradient intensity below this value are discarded.

EdgeDetectionSobelSettings.description:
Extracts directional boundaries by computing spatial image intensity gradients.

This algorithm applies localized 3x3 kernels to approximate the first derivative
of pixel intensities across the horizontal and vertical axes. It highlights
areas of sharp luminance changes, producing a continuous gradient map that
emphasizes prominent structural edges and surface transitions.

kernelSize.description:
The size of the Sobel operator window.

Typically 3. Larger values (5, 7) provide a more smoothed
gradient but result in "thicker" edges. Must be an odd number.

EnhanceContrastSettings.description:
Configuration for contrast enhancement and histogram manipulation.

This algorithm can perform linear contrast stretching, normalization,
or histogram equalization to improve the dynamic range of an image.

equalizeHistogram.description:
Whether to apply Histogram Equalization.

This redistributes pixel intensities to achieve a uniform distribution,
which is highly effective for images with low contrast but high noise.

normalize.description:
Whether to linearly stretch the remaining pixel intensities to fill
the full [0.0, 1.0] range.

saturatedPixels.description:
Percentage of pixels to "clip" from the top and bottom of the histogram.

In percent (0 - 100), split evenly between the darkest and the
brightest pixels, like ImageJ: 0.35 clips 0.175 % at each end. A small
value (ImageJ's default is 0.35) ignores hot/dead pixels that would
otherwise prevent effective contrast stretching.

ExcludeImageSettings.description:
Leaves an image out of the results when its measurements say it's bad.

Each rule compares a measurement of an earlier step (e.g. Image
Quality's focus score) with a value. When the rules are met, the image
is analysed to the end but disabled in the results, with the reason - to
check it by hand and enable it again if it's fine. The rules are checked
on every plane; one plane meeting them excludes the whole image. A
measurement without a value (e.g. the slope of a flat image) doesn't
meet a rule.

excludeWhen.description: Excluded when one rule is met, or only when all of them are.

rules.description: The rules: a measurement below or above a value.

ExcludeRuleSettings.description: One rule: a measurement compared with a value.

comparison.description: Met when the measurement is below or above the value.

measurement.description: The measurement, made by an earlier step.

value.description: The value, in the measurement's unit.

ExtractClassMappingSettings.description: The object class the objects of one segmentation class get.

objectClass.description:
The object class its objects get: a project class, or inside a
module one of the module's own classes.

segmentationClass.description: The segmentation class, as set by Threshold, Pixel classifier, ...

ExtractObjectsSettings.description:
Represents a bounded object extracted from a labeled image.
A command to extract spatial statistics and bounding boxes from labeled objects.

classMapping.description:
Which object class the objects of a segmentation class get.

Without an entry, a segmentation class's objects get the project class
with the same number - what the Threshold's class choice means. Inside
a module, map to one of the module's own classes to keep the
objects internal to the module.

maxObjectsBeforeFail.description:
Maximum allowed ROIs to extract.

If this limit is exceeded the pipeline fails.
This is a protection against memory overload.

FillHolesSettings.description:
Fills enclosed background holes in the segmentation map.

[Preprocessing] -> [Segment/Threshold] -> [Fill Holes] -> [Connected Components] -> [Watershed] -> [Extract Objects]

A direct port of ImageJ's `Process > Binary > Fill Holes` command
(`ij.plugin.filter.Binary.fill`, originally contributed by Gabriel
Landini): a background pixel counts as a "hole" - and is turned into
foreground - exactly when it cannot be reached from the image border by a
path of background pixels using 4-connectivity.

Which pixels count as a "hole" is decided the same way ImageJ does it:
every non-background pixel is "foreground" regardless of its actual
label/class value, so a background pocket enclosed by *any* mix of labels
is still a hole. Unlike ImageJ, each hole is then attributed back to the
class that actually encloses it - every enclosed background region is
grouped into a connected component, and that component is filled with
whichever label is most common among its immediately bordering pixels
(falling back to `FILL_VALUE` only in the degenerate case of a hole with
no foreground neighbor at all). This keeps multi-class segmentation maps
correct: a hole inside a class-2 object is filled with 2, not merged with
a fixed value that happens to collide with an unrelated class elsewhere
in the image.

FillObjectHolesSettings.description:
Fills the holes inside every object, one object at a time.

[AI Cellpose / StarDist Segmentation | Watershed | Connected Components] -> [Fill Object Holes] -> [Extract Objects]

Works on the objects (instance map), so it has to come after a step that
creates objects and before Extract Objects. A pixel becomes part of an
object when it is enclosed by that object alone; a gap enclosed by several
touching objects together is left as it is. An object lying completely
inside another object's hole becomes part of the enclosing object. Filled
pixels get the class of the object they now belong to.

Use Fill Holes instead to fill holes in the segmentation map before the
objects are created (e.g. right after a Threshold).

FiltersHessianHessianModeSettings.description:
Specifies the feature extraction method for the Hessian matrix.

The Hessian matrix describes the local second-order structure of an image,
often used for blob detection (LoG) or ridge extraction.

oneOf.description:
Computes the determinant: $det(H) = I_{xx}I_{yy} - I_{xy}^2$.

High values typically indicate "blob-like" structures or corners.

Extracts the first (larger) eigenvalue ($\lambda_1$).

Useful for detecting the maximum local curvature, identifying
the principal axis of a ridge.

Extracts the second (smaller) eigenvalue ($\lambda_2$).

Highlights secondary curvature; when both $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$
are large, it indicates a blob or interest point.

FiltersIlluminationCorrectionApplyMethod.description: How the estimated illumination field is combined with the original image.

oneOf.description:
`corrected = image * mean(field) / field`. Multiplicative correction
that preserves overall image brightness - the right default for
gain/vignetting-style illumination problems.
`corrected = image - (field - mean(field))`. Additive correction.

FiltersIlluminationCorrectionCorrectionM.description: How the illumination field is estimated from the block-reduced image.

oneOf.description:
Block *mean*. The right default for typical uneven illumination
(vignetting, uneven excitation): every block contributes its average
brightness to the estimated field.

Block *minimum*. Use this when dense or bright foreground objects
would otherwise pull the mean-based estimate upward - the minimum
hugs the true background floor instead.

FiltersIlluminationCorrectionSmoothingMe.description:
Smoothing applied to the block-reduced field to remove blockiness before
it is used as the correction field.

oneOf.description: Use the block-reduced field as-is.
Separable Gaussian blur of the block grid.
Windowed median filter of the block grid.

Fits a smooth 2nd-order polynomial surface
(a + bx + cy + dx² + exy + fy²) through the block grid. Has no
tunable radius/sigma, so it's the most stable option when unsure.

FiltersIntensityTransformIntensityTransf.description: Specifies how intensity adjustments are calculated.

oneOf.description: Parameters are calculated based on image statistics (e.g., histogram analysis).
Parameters are provided explicitly by the user.

FiltersRankFilterRankFilterTypeSettings.description: Specifies the statistical operation to perform on the local pixel neighborhood.

oneOf.description:
Selects the middle value. Excellent for removing salt-and-pepper noise
while preserving sharp edges.

Selects the lowest intensity (Erosion). Shrinks bright regions and
expands dark regions.

Selects the highest intensity (Dilation). Expands bright regions and
shrinks dark regions.

Computes the average value. Acts as a box blur, smoothing the image
but blurring edges.

Replaces a pixel only if it deviates from the neighborhood median
by more than the specified threshold.

FiltersRollingBallBallTypeSettings.description: The geometric shape used to probe the image intensity surface.

oneOf.description:
A spherical cap.

This is the traditional ImageJ algorithm. Best for images with
distinct, round features like cells or particles.

A sliding parabolic surface.

Mathematically smoother at the edges than the Ball, often
resulting in fewer artifacts on complex gradients.

FiltersStructureTensorTensorModeSettings.description: The specific calculation to extract from the Structure Tensor.

oneOf.description:
Extracts the first (primary) eigenvalue.

Represents the local image intensity variation in the direction
perpendicular to the edge. Useful for edge detection.

Extracts the second (secondary) eigenvalue.

Represents the local image intensity variation along the edge.
High values typically indicate corners or noise.

Computes the local anisotropy (coherence) of the image.

Measures how strongly the local neighborhood is oriented.
Ranges from 0 (isotropic/noise) to 1 (perfectly oriented/straight edge).

GaussianBlurSettings.description:
Smooths an image and reduces background noise using a Gaussian kernel.

This algorithm applies a localized, bell-curve weighted blur that suppresses
high-frequency pixel variations (like camera noise, salt-and-pepper artifacts,
or dust) while preserving structural features. It is commonly used as a
preprocessing step to optimize thresholding and edge detection tasks.

kernelSize.description:
The size of the blur matrix.

Must be an odd number (e.g., 3, 5, 7).

sigma.description:
The standard deviation of the Gaussian kernel.

Higher values create a more significant blur effect.
$$N \approx 6\sigma + 1$$

GroupingMode.description: How images are grouped into wells.

oneOf.description:
The well-name pattern is detected from the image names (e.g.
`A01_01.tif`, `Exp_B3_s2.tif`).
`PlateSettings::grouping_regex` on the image name.

One well per image folder - placed on the plate when the folder is
named like a well (`B03/`).

HessianSettings.description:
Extracts continuous structural ridges, tubular vessels, and blobs using second-order spatial derivatives.

This algorithm constructs a localized Hessian matrix for each pixel to analyze local curvature
and intensity topography. By evaluating the eigenvalues of this matrix, it differentiates
between directional ridges (like blood vessels or filaments), distinct intensity peaks (blobs),
and flat regions, making it highly effective for curvilinear feature extraction.

mode.description:
Determines which component of the Hessian matrix structure to extract.

Depending on the mode, this can highlight interest points (blobs)
or directional features (ridges).

HsvRangeSettings.description:
Defines a range within the HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) color space.

This is commonly used for color-based filtering or "chroma keying."

IlluminationCorrectionSettings.description:
Use this when your images are brighter in the middle and dimmer toward
the edges/corners (vignetting), or show any other smooth shading pattern
that repeats the same way across every tile or every image from the same
microscope/camera setup - a consequence of the optics or illumination,
not the sample. Left uncorrected, that shading makes intensity
comparisons between regions of an image (or between images/wells)
unreliable, even though it rarely stops segmentation from finding
objects on its own.

Use **Rolling Ball** instead when the problem is a
*local* background glow or halo under/around individual objects (e.g.
out-of-focus light, autofluorescence, uneven staining) that differs from
image to image rather than being tied to the acquisition setup -
RollingBall strips that local floor so thresholding/segmentation works
cleanly. The two solve different problems: RollingBall won't fix a
global brightness gradient, and this filter won't remove a local halo.

### How it works

Flat-field ("illumination") correction: estimates a smooth, slowly-varying
gain/offset field caused by uneven illumination (vignetting, dust on the
condenser, uneven excitation) and removes it in a single calculate+apply
step - equivalent to CellProfiler's `CorrectIlluminationCalculate` and
`CorrectIlluminationApply` modules combined into one.

Unlike `RollingBall`, which estimates a *local* per-object background
baseline via a rolling structural element, this estimates one *global*,
low-frequency field for the whole image/channel.

applyMethod.description: How the field is combined with the original image.

blockSize.description:
Block size, in pixels, used to reduce the image to a coarse
illumination estimate before smoothing. Should be larger than the
largest foreground object, so objects are averaged/eroded away and
only the slow-varying illumination trend survives.

method.description: How the illumination field is estimated from the image.

rescale.description:
Stretch the corrected image's intensities to fill the full
`[0.0, 1.0]` range afterward - guards against `Divide` pushing
previously-dim regions above `1.0`.

smoothing.description: Smoothing applied to the block-reduced field to remove blockiness.

oneOf.description:
No image - only as a pipeline's start: its first step loads one
(Load Image Channel, Image Cache Load).

ImageCacheSettings.description:
A filter that acts as a synchronization point between the pipeline and a storage backend.

`ImageCache` allows the pipeline to branch or "undo" operations by saving
states to a named address and reloading them as needed.

address.description: The unique identifier or memory slot where the image is stored.

mode.description: Whether to save the current state to the cache or load a state from it.

ImageChannelIdx.description:
0-based index of an image channel, as a command setting. Shown in the
pipeline UI as the channel picker (channel name + color of the open
image). Serializes as a plain number, so it can replace an existing
integer channel field without breaking saved projects.

ImageMathSettings.description:
A filter that performs pixel-wise mathematical operations between the current
pipeline image and a secondary image stored in the cache.

This command allows for complex image blending, masking, and comparison.

operand.description: The specific mathematical or logical operator to apply.

secondImageAddress.description: The second image to use for the operation.

swapOperands.description:
If false, the calculation is `(Current Image OP Cached Image)`.
If true, the calculation is `(Cached Image OP Current Image)`.

This is critical for non-commutative operations like Subtraction or Division.

IntensityFilterSettings.description:
One intensity criterion of [`ClassifyObjects`], e.g. "average intensity
in channel 1 brighter than 1200".

channel.description:
Image channel whose intensity is compared (0-based)

An object without a measurement for this channel (the image has no
such channel) never matches.

comparison.description: Whether the object must be brighter or darker than the threshold

metric.description: Intensity statistic of the object to compare

threshold.description:
Intensity threshold, in `unit`

For `Sum` this is the summed intensity of all object pixels, so it
scales with the object's area.

unit.description:
Unit of `threshold`

bit: gray value, 0 - 255/65535 (as in ImageJ/Fiji)
%: 0 - 100.0
rel: 0 - 1.0

IntensityTransformationSettings.description:
Configuration for adjusting image contrast and brightness.

This transformation applies a linear mapping to pixel values.
In manual mode, the output is typically calculated as:
`output = input * contrast + brightness`.

brightness.description:
Brightness offset (bias).

Only active in manual mode.
Positive values brighten the image, negative values darken it.

contrast.description:
Contrast multiplier (gain).

Only active in manual mode.
Values > 1.0 increase contrast, while values < 1.0 decrease it.

mode.description: Determines whether to use automated enhancement or user-defined values.

LaplacianSettings.description:
Configuration for the Laplacian edge detection filter.

The Laplacian is a second-order derivative operator used to find regions of
rapid intensity change. It is particularly effective for detecting edges
and fine details, though it is highly sensitive to noise.

kernelSize.description:
The size of the discrete Laplacian aperture.

Typically 3. Larger sizes (5, 7) approximate the Laplacian of Gaussian (LoG)
more closely but are more computationally expensive. Must be an odd number.

LoadAnnotatedObjectsSettings.description:
Loads the hand-annotated objects of the image into the pipeline.

Every loaded object gets a new object id, is marked as manually annotated
and has its intensities measured on every channel - from there on it is
handled like any segmented object.

inputClasses.description:
Only load annotations carrying at least one of these classes.

Leave empty to load every annotated object of the image.

keepAnnotatedClasses.description:
Keep the classes the objects were given while annotating.

Turn off to start from `output_class` alone.

outputClass.description:
Class added to every loaded object, so later steps can select them.
Set to `Unset` to add none.

useOn.description:
On which planes an annotation is used: where it was drawn, or on
every plane (and time point) - e.g. a region outlined once.

LoadChannelSettings.description:
Loads an image channel as the image the following steps work on.

Replaces the current image. Use it as the first step of a pipeline
without an image source, or to switch channels within a pipeline - e.g.
a module that detects nuclei in one channel and cells in another.

Projection: Auto loads the channel as the project's z-stack setting does.
Any other choice loads it with its own z-projection, or one z-plane (None).
Use it with a project that analyzes one projection or one plane: if the project analyzes the z-planes one by one, the pipeline runs once per plane on the same image and its objects repeat for every plane.
Objects found on another projection are still drawn over the project's image, and annotations are matched to the project's z-planes.

projection.description:
Optional z projection setting

If set to Auto the global z-projection setting from the project is used.
If not Auto the image channel is loaded with the given z-projection settings.

zIndex.description: With projection None: the z-plane loaded (0 = the first).

MathImageCacheImageCacheModeSettings.description: Defines the interaction type with the persistent image storage.

oneOf.description:
Captures the current image from the pipeline and writes it to the cache.

Used for "checkpointing" results at a specific stage in the pipeline
for later comparison or retrieval.

Retrieves a previously stored image from the cache and injects it
into the current pipeline context.

This effectively replaces the current working image with the cached version.

MathImageMathOperandSettings.description: The mathematical or logical operation to perform between two images.

oneOf.description: No operation; typically used as a placeholder.
Unary operation: Negates the intensities of the primary image.
Arithmetic addition: `A + B`. (Clamped to the maximum pixel value).
Arithmetic subtraction: `A - B`. (Clamped to zero).
Arithmetic multiplication: `A * B`.
Arithmetic division: `A / B`.
Bitwise AND operation.
Bitwise OR operation.
Bitwise XOR operation.
Per-pixel minimum: `min(A, B)`. (Darkest Pixel).
Per-pixel maximum: `max(A, B)`. (Brightest Pixel).
Arithmetic mean: `(A + B) / 2`.
Absolute difference: `|A - B|`. Useful for change detection.

MeasureColocalizationCostesMethodSetting.description:
How Costes' automatic thresholds are searched for (CellProfiler's
"Method for Costes thresholding").

oneOf.description: No Costes values.

A shrinking window of candidates - a few passes over the image, also
for 16-bit images (CellProfiler's "Faster").

Candidates from the top down, skipping while far off (CellProfiler's
"Fast" - slow on 16-bit images).

Every candidate from the top down (CellProfiler's "Accurate" - very
slow on 16-bit images).
One rule met is enough.
Every rule must be met.

MeasureExcludeImageRuleComparisonSetting.description: Which side of the value meets a rule.

oneOf.description: Met below the value (e.g. a focus score too low).
Met above the value (e.g. too many saturated pixels).

MeasureImageAreaOccupiedSettings.description:
Measures how much of the image the objects of a class cover.

The area in pixels and µm² (with a known pixel size) and the part of the
image (0..1). Where objects overlap, the area counts once.

id.description:
The step's ID, unique in the project - its values' keys start with
it ("area_occupied_01/...").

objectClass.description: The objects whose area is measured.

MeasureImageColocalizationSettings.description:
Measures how two channels go together over the whole image -
CellProfiler's MeasureColocalization, per image.

Pearson (-1 to 1) uses every pixel. Manders M1 is the part of channel
A's intensity where channel B is bright too (M2 the other way round),
"bright" meaning above the threshold - a percentage of the channel's
maximum, or Costes' automatic threshold. The overlap coefficient, K1/K2
and RWC (Manders weighted by how similar the two pixels' ranks are) use
the same pixels.

costes.description: Manders with Costes' automatic thresholds, and how they are found.

id.description:
The step's ID, unique in the project - its values' keys start with
it ("coloc_01/...").

thresholdPercent.description:
A pixel counts for Manders, the overlap and RWC when it is brighter
than this percentage of its channel's maximum (in the image).

MeasureImageIntensitySettings.description:
Measures the brightness of a channel across the whole image.

Total, mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, median, lower and
upper quartile and median absolute deviation - in gray values, like the
objects' intensities. It uses every pixel of the image, the background
too.

id.description:
The step's ID, unique in the project - its values' keys start with
it ("intensity_01/...").

MeasureImageQualitySettings.description:
Measures how usable a channel of the image is: sharp, not noisy, not
overexposed.

Focus score (the variance over the mean - low: blurry), power log-log
slope (how fast fine detail fades - more negative: blurrier), the
percent of pixels at the image's maximum and minimum (high: saturated or
clipped) - all as CellProfiler gives them - and the noise (σ in gray
values, Immerkær's estimate). Use them with "Exclude Image" to leave bad
images out of the results.

id.description:
The step's ID, unique in the project - its values' keys start with
it ("quality_01/...").

MeasureImageTextureSettings.description:
Measures the texture of a channel over the whole image - Haralick's
features (CellProfiler's MeasureTexture, per image).

The pixel pairs the scale apart in a direction say how the gray levels
go together: e.g. contrast is high where neighbours differ a lot, the
angular second moment where few pairs repeat over and over (smooth or
regular), entropy where the pairs are all different.

directions.description:
One value per feature (the mean of the directions) or one per
direction.

grayLevels.description:
The gray levels the 8-bit values are rescaled to (2 to 256): fewer
are faster and less noisy, more see finer differences.

id.description:
The step's ID, unique in the project - its values' keys start with
it ("texture_01/...").

scale.description:
How far apart the two pixels of a pair are, in pixels - about the
size of the texture's grain.

MeasureObjectColocalizationSettings.description:
Measures how two channels go together in each object of a class -
CellProfiler's MeasureColocalization, per object.

The values of Measure Image Colocalization (but the slope) of the
object's pixels: the threshold is a percentage of the object's maximum,
RWC ranks the values of all the objects, and Costes uses the whole
image's Costes thresholds.

costes.description:
Manders with Costes' automatic thresholds (the whole image's), and
how they are found.

id.description:
The step's ID, unique in the project - its values' keys start with
it ("object_coloc_01/...").

thresholdPercent.description:
A pixel counts for Manders, the overlap and RWC when it is brighter
than this percentage of its channel's maximum (in the object).

MeasureObjectDistanceToParentSettings.description:
Each child's distance to its parent of a class (linked by Relate
Objects): centre to centre, and from its centre to the parent's edge.
A child without a parent of the class has no value.

id.description:
The step's ID, unique in the project - its values' keys start with
it ("parent_distance_01/...").

parentClass.description: The class of their parent (as linked by Relate Objects, e.g. Cell).

MeasureObjectNeighborsNeighborMethodSett.description:
Which objects count as neighbours (CellProfiler's "Method to determine
neighbors").

oneOf.description:
Every object first grows over the background until it meets the
others; then the ones it touches.
The objects it touches (1 px apart at most).
The objects within the distance.

MeasureObjectNeighborsSettings.description:
For each object: its neighbours, how much of its outline touches them,
and its first and second closest object.

The closest objects are by the distance between the centres; each
distance names the object it is to. "Percent touching" is the part of
the object's outline pixels within the distance (+ ½ px) of a neighbour.

distance.description: With "Within a distance": how far, in pixels.

id.description:
The step's ID, unique in the project - its values' keys start with
it ("neighbors_01/...").

neighbors.description:
The objects that count as neighbours (unset: the measured objects
themselves).

MeasureObjectShapeSettings.description:
For each object: its convex area and solidity as CellProfiler gives them
(the pixels whose centre lies in the convex hull; area / convex area),
its Euler number (1 - holes, 8-connected) and its radii (the distance of
its pixels to the nearest pixel outside it: maximum, mean, median).

id.description:
The step's ID, unique in the project - its values' keys start with
it ("shape_01/...").

MeasureObjectTextureSettings.description:
Measures the texture of a channel in each object of a class - Haralick's
features (CellProfiler's MeasureTexture, per object).

The same values as Measure Image Texture, of the object's pixels only.

directions.description:
One value per feature (the mean of the directions) or one per
direction.

grayLevels.description:
The gray levels the 8-bit values are rescaled to (2 to 256): fewer
are faster and less noisy, more see finer differences.

id.description:
The step's ID, unique in the project - its values' keys start with
it ("object_texture_01/...").

scale.description:
How far apart the two pixels of a pair are, in pixels - about the
size of the texture's grain.

MeasureTextureTextureDirectionsSettings.description:
Which values per feature: the mean of the four directions, or one per
direction.

oneOf.description: The mean of the four directions - one value per feature.

A value per direction (0°, 45°, 90°, 135°), as CellProfiler stores
them - four times as many values.

MedianSubtractSettings.description:
A background subtraction filter that uses a median rank operator.

This algorithm is highly effective for removing large-scale background
variations while preserving small, high-contrast features. It works by
estimating the background as the median intensity within a local radius.

radius.description:
The radius of the neighborhood used to estimate the background.

Features smaller than this radius will be preserved, while
larger structures will be treated as background and removed.

appVersion.description:
Version of EVAnalyzer that last wrote this file (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`
of the writing build). Empty for files written before this field
existed, or built by hand rather than saved from the app.

authors.description:
Every author, in display order (the first entry is treated as the
primary author in template/pipeline picker dialogs, the rest as
co-authors). Free-form display strings, not split into first/last.

category.description: Category used to group templates in pickers (e.g. "Cell Biology / Uptake")

description.description: A long detailed description of the module

shortDescription.description: A short one line description of the module

tags.description: Free-form keywords used to search/filter templates

version.description: The author's version of this module or template

ModuleDefinition.description: A module as defined in the project: its steps and the parameters it shows.

classes.description: Local classes used by the module. These classes are scoped to the module only

origin.description:
The library file this definition was inserted from, if any. Not
written when absent, so library files (`.evamodule`) never carry it.

parameters.description: The module's parameters, shown on the module card.

steps.description: The steps which are executed in the given order

ModuleInstance.description: A use of a module in a pipeline: which definition, with which values.

key.description: The module's key in the project.

values.description:
This instance's parameter values. A parameter missing here has its
definition's default (e.g. one the definition gained later).

contentHash.description:
A fingerprint of the definition as inserted - if it differs now, the

replace those changes. Empty in files written before.

originModuleKey.description:
If this is a copy form an existing module, this is the origin module key.
This allows to reset the module default settings.

version.description: The definition's version in that file when it was inserted.

ModuleParamKey.description:
A module parameter's key, unique within its module definition and
readable in the file (`"min_size"`). The values a module instance holds
are keyed by it, so they survive reordering and relabelling the
definition's parameters, and updating it from the library. Made from the
